newsitem.title: ZAMBIA: Zambia banks on renewed aid for budget surplus.
newsitem.headline: Zambia banks on renewed aid for budget surplus.

text.p: Zambia is aiming for a budget surplus in 1997, banking on a resumption of normal aid flows from Western donors, Finance Minister Ronald Penza said on Friday.
Presenting the national budget to parliament, Penza said the government expected to have 1,489.1 billion kwacha ($1.1 billion) in revenue against the projected expenditure of 1,427.1 billion kwacha.
"About two thirds of total expenditure will be financed from internal financial resources," he said, adding that foreign aid would account for 488.9 billion kwacha.
Of the donor component 358.9 billion kwacha will be project support and 130 billion non-project support.
Penza said preliminary indications were that Zambia would need around $200 million in balance of payment support and about $275 million in project financing.
"We are hopeful that we can obtain the remaining commitment from our cooperating partners in the spirit of true partnership and mutual respect," he said.
Penza said the intended budget surplus would be used to pay the government's domestic debts.

Western donors cut aid to Zambia last year after constitutional amendments by President Frederick Chiluba barred his main opponents from contesting a general election which he later won in a landslide.
